transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-21
Time: 09:30 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Nina Park (Redwood CSM); Priya Kapoor (NexaHead - Head of ML), Ethan Chen (Eng Manager), Maya Singh (Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly check-in for the pilot onboarding: access, environment readiness, and next steps for running benchmarks. POC continues toward testing Hosted and Dedicated configurations; customer needs staging network access and security signoffs.

Topics:
- Staging access and service account / keys
- VPC peering and firewall rules
- KMS/HSM and data encryption requirements
- Benchmark plan (latency/cost) across model variants and quantization profiles
- Timeline for dedicated capacity scoping

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we can do a quick 45 today, agenda is access, env readiness, and benchmark plan. sound good?
[00:08] Priya: yeah that's perfect, we've got Ethan and Maya here to help with infra and security.
[00:12] Ethan: morning, quick note we tried the sample curl but hit a TLS error when we tried from staging.
[00:20] Diego: ok that's likely the network egress or the service account wasn't set up; Jordan i shared a checklist last week, i'll reattach it after. there are a couple of required ports and the IP ranges for Redwood Hosted + Dedicated nodes.
[00:32] Maya: also we need confirmation on KMS integration — our compliance team requires customer-managed keys for any PHI-like data. does Redwood Private support HSM/KMS?
[00:44] Jordan: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS and can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM, we'll share the integration doc. for Hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer keys via our KMS bridge but Private is the fully isolated option.
[00:56] Priya: we're mostly aiming to start on Hosted to get quick signals, then move to Dedicated if the latency/cost profile makes sense.
[01:03] Diego: perfect — for benchmarks we recommend running both Hosted and a small Dedicated profile. we'll test with the same request mix + sequence lengths. i'll put together a script that runs 1k requests across short/med/long sequences and measures p95 latency and tokens/sec.
[01:18] Ethan: what's your expectation for p95? our SLA target is under 200ms for short queries, but we understand longer sequences will be higher.
[01:25] Diego: for short prompts on our curated 7B-like models you should see ~120-180ms p95 on Dedicated; Hosted varies with multi-tenant load but typically within 1.5x. i'll mark that as a goal but the benchmark will give concrete numbers.
[01:39] Priya: one more constraint — we don't want requests to leave our region (EU vs US) for data residency reasons, how do we pin region?
[01:46] Jordan: we can route to EU region endpoints; for Private we'd deploy in your VPC/region. for Hosted we can ensure region pinning in the request meta, we'll include region routing docs.
[01:58] Maya: about audit logs — we need request-level logs with user identifiers retained for 90 days. do you have that?
[02:05] Nina: yes, Redwood console has per-token tracing and request logs; retention is configurable as an add-on, we'll include the retention SLA and export options.
[02:15] Ethan: back to the TLS issue, i can share logs in the chat. we did a curl from the staging bastion to the redwood-hosted endpoint and saw CERT_UNKNOWN maybe the cert chain was missing.
[02:25] Diego: that can happen if the intermediate chain isn't present or if corporate proxy rewrites. Ethan can you try with --verbose and drop the output. Jordan i'll follow up with the IP ranges and CA chain we expect.
[02:38] Priya: ok on benchmark scheduling — we want the baseline before end of month. can you run the benchmark against our dev dataset? it has similar token distribution but not PHI.
[02:48] Jordan: yes, Diego will run the script against your dev dataset. we'll need a service account with read access and an endpoint URL; Ethan if you can provision the service account and send creds to the secure drop we'll do the rest.
[02:58] Maya: security note — creds must be rotated and not embedded in code. we prefer short-lived tokens via STS where possible.
[03:05] Diego: we support short-lived tokens and can wire up STS workflows; if you prefer we can use a temporary service account for the benchmark.
[03:12] Ethan: i'll open a ticket to provision a service account and let you know when it's ready, target EOD tomorrow.
[03:18] Priya: on quality — we saw some hallucination on our fine-tune from a small dataset; any tuning suggestions?
[03:25] Diego: yep, two levers: instruction-tuning + prompt engineering and fallback chains (rerankers). we can tune temperature/top-p and use ranking with embeddings to reduce hallucination. also quantization profile affects generation subtly; we'll note that in the benchmark results.
[03:38] Priya: do you support hybrid routing so we can fall back to a safer model variant if the primary's confidence is low?
[03:44] Jordan: yes, Redwood supports smart routing — you can configure policy-based fallbacks to smaller or more conservative variants, and we can A/B the rollouts via the Console.
[03:53] Priya: sounds good. for the POC success criteria: 1) p95 latency under 250ms for short queries on Hosted or within 1.5x of Dedicated, 2) cost projection under $X per 1M tokens (we'll agree on the number after benchmarks), 3) security signoff for encryption/logging. we can formalize after the benchmark.
[04:13] Jordan: great, that's aligned. i'll recap action items at the end.
[04:18] Ethan: quick question on pricing — if we move to Dedicated monthly commit, how fast can we scale up?
[04:24] Jordan: Dedicated pools are configurable; initial commit can be sized for baseline throughput and we can enable burst capacity. we'll scope exact numbers on the dedicated scoping call.
[04:33] Maya: also share the security pack (SOC2 certs, ISO docs) so our legal team can start review.
[04:38] Nina: we'll attach the security pack and the KMS/HSM integration guide after the call.
[04:44] Priya: thanks, that would help.
[04:46] Jordan: ok quick recap of next steps — Diego will prepare and run the benchmark script and share results (due 2027-07-26), Jordan will send the staging access checklist and IP ranges (due 2027-07-22), Ethan will provision service account and confirm VPC/firewall details (due 2027-07-28), Maya will share compliance acceptance criteria (due 2027-07-27). we'll schedule a dedicated scoping call for the week of 2027-08-02.
[05:03] Priya: thanks everyone, see you next week.

End of transcript.
